content.title:
Scored quiz
Module 1
content.intro: This quiz covers all the lessons in this module. You must achieve 80% to pass. Good luck!

questions.prompt: What percent of global greenhouse gas emissions can be attributed to energy production and use?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Energy is the dominant contributor to climate change, so much so, that reaching zero carbon emissions is dependent on an energy transition and leapfrogging historic energy development pathways.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Energy is the dominant contributor to climate change, so much so, that reaching zero carbon emissions is dependent on an energy transition and leapfrogging historic energy development pathways.

questions.prompt: What relationship does energy have with HDI?

options.value: Human development increases energy production and consumption

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Energy and HDI have a relationship similar to the chicken and the egg - it is unclear which factor influences the other, disproving a causal relationship. However, we know that increased energy consumption leads to higher HDI, and higher HDI leads to increased energy production and consumption.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Energy and HDI have a relationship similar to the chicken and the egg - it is unclear which factor influences the other, disproving a causal relationship. However, we know that increased energy consumption leads to higher HDI, and higher HDI leads to increased energy production and consumption.

questions.prompt: How does energy access increase gender equality?

options.value: Reducing time poverty for women and girls
Increasing men's employment opportunities in the renewable energy sector
Increasing security for women and girls

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Women and girls are believed, in some regions, to be spending up to 18 hours weekly on wood gathering and household cooking (UNDP, 2022). Therefore, access to clean energy directly aids in reducing women's time poverty. Public outdoor lighting increases security for women and girls, allowing more autonomy after dark and reducing exposure to gender-based violence.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Women and girls are believed, in some regions, to be spending up to 18 hours weekly on wood gathering and household cooking (UNDP, 2022). Therefore, access to clean energy directly aids in reducing women's time poverty. Public outdoor lighting increases security for women and girls, allowing more autonomy after dark and reducing exposure to gender-based violence.

questions.prompt: How efficient is the global energy system?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: The current global energy system operates at only 37% efficiency (RMI, 2019), meaning that nearly two-thirds of the primary energy produced is lost due to inefficiencies in generation, transportation, and end-use.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: The current global energy system operates at only 37% efficiency (RMI, 2019), meaning that nearly two-thirds of the primary energy produced is lost due to inefficiencies in generation, transportation, and end-use.

questions.prompt: What is the largest source of renewable energy in the Arab States region?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Hydropower plays a dominant role in the Arab States. While 7% of power flows from renewable sources, about 3.4% comes specifically from hydropower. It has the largest installed capacity at 11.2 GW.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Hydropower plays a dominant role in the Arab States. While 7% of power flows from renewable sources, about 3.4% comes specifically from hydropower. It has the largest installed capacity at 11.2 GW.

questions.prompt: Which region has the largest energy access gap?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Africa is the region with the largest gap in energy access. With over 80% of Africa’s unelectrified population in rural areas, off-grid and decentralized renewable energy solutions can both grant access and leapfrog traditional development pathways.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Africa is the region with the largest gap in energy access. With over 80% of Africa’s unelectrified population in rural areas, off-grid and decentralized renewable energy solutions can both grant access and leapfrog traditional development pathways.

questions.prompt: Which renewable energy export from the Eastern Europe and Central Asia region could be positively affected by the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Hydrogen presents a growing energy opportunity for the RBEC region, despite currently negligible export levels under the chemicals category. With the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) increasing costs for carbon-intensive exports, there is strong incentive to decarbonize. EU initiatives like REPowerEU are supporting countries such as Moldova, Ukraine, and those in the Western Balkans to invest in producing and trading clean fuels, including renewable hydrogen, positioning hydrogen as a critical future export and energy solution to meet rising EU demand

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Hydrogen presents a growing energy opportunity for the RBEC region, despite currently negligible export levels under the chemicals category. With the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) increasing costs for carbon-intensive exports, there is strong incentive to decarbonize. EU initiatives like REPowerEU are supporting countries such as Moldova, Ukraine, and those in the Western Balkans to invest in producing and trading clean fuels, including renewable hydrogen, positioning hydrogen as a critical future export and energy solution to meet rising EU demand

questions.prompt: Who would be included in a whole-of-society approach to the energy transition?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: A whole-of-society approach (WoS) to energy transition involves not just governments and energy companies but also policymakers, businesses, financial institutions, civil society, academia, Indigenous communities, and the general public, ensuring that diverse perspectives shape energy policies and projects.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: A whole-of-society approach (WoS) to energy transition involves not just governments and energy companies but also policymakers, businesses, financial institutions, civil society, academia, Indigenous communities, and the general public, ensuring that diverse perspectives shape energy policies and projects.

questions.prompt: What is a key reason that increased investment in resilient energy infrastructure is essential for Caribbean countries?

options.value: Because they have stable weather conditions
Because natural disasters frequently damage energy systems

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Caribbean states spend up to 1.2% of GDP on natural disaster recovery annually. Resilient infrastructure – especially solar mini-grids – can protect critical services during disasters.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Caribbean states spend up to 1.2% of GDP on natural disaster recovery annually. Resilient infrastructure – especially solar mini-grids – can protect critical services during disasters.

questions.prompt: Why is the development of green hydrogen considered a major opportunity for countries like Chile, Uruguay, and Brazil?

options.value: These countries lack other renewable energy sources
Green hydrogen reduces fossil fuel subsidies
It allows for energy storage and clean export industries
It eliminates the need for wind and solar power

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Green hydrogen can be produced using abundant low-cost solar and wind resources in these countries and then exported as a clean fuel

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Green hydrogen can be produced using abundant low-cost solar and wind resources in these countries and then exported as a clean fuel
